verses.1: I raised my eyes and saw — behold, four horns.
verses.2: I asked the angel speaking to me, "What are these?" He said to me, "These are the horns that have scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem."
verses.3: Then the Lord showed me four craftsmen.
verses.4: I asked, "What are these coming to do?" He said, "These are the craftsmen who have counteracted the horns that scattered Judah. Each of them struck down a horn of the nations that had raised their horns against the land of Judah to scatter it."
verses.5: I raised my eyes again and saw — behold, a man holding a measuring line.
verses.6: I asked, "Where are you going?" He said to me, "To measure Jerusalem to see how wide and how long it is."
verses.7: Then the angel speaking to me was going out, and another angel was coming out to meet him.
verses.8: He said to him, "Run and tell that young man, 'Jerusalem will be inhabited in fullness, with many people and cattle in its midst.'"
verses.9: I myself will be its wall of fire all around, and I will be its glory within," says the Lord.
verses.10: "Ho! Ho! Flee from the land of the north," says the Lord. "For I am scattering you in all the four winds of heaven," says the Lord.
verses.11: "Ho, Zion! Escape, you who dwell in the daughter of Babylon."
verses.12: For thus says the Lord of Hosts: "After glory I have sent me to the nations that have plundered you, for whoever touches you touches the apple of my eye."
verses.13: "For behold, I will lift my hand against them, and they will become plunder for their servants. And you will know that the Lord of Hosts has sent me to you."
verses.14: "Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Zion, for behold, I am coming and I will dwell in your midst," says the Lord.
verses.15: "Many nations will come to the Lord on that day, and they will become my people. I will dwell among you, and you will know that the Lord of Hosts has sent me to you."
verses.16: "The Lord will claim Judah as his inheritance; it is his portion on the holy land. And he will yet choose Jerusalem again."
verses.17: "Let all flesh tremble before the Lord, for he has stirred himself from his holy dwelling."

notes:
Notes
- v. 4: The Hebrew uses "לִקְרָאתֽוֹ" for "to meet him," which can mean "to face him" or "to confront him." The context of divine judgment suggests "to confront him" is more appropriate.
- v. 17: "מִמְּעוֹן קָדְשֽׁוֹ" is translated as "his holy dwelling" to reflect the source text's reference to the Lord's sacred place.
